question: True or false: most Silk Road goods were carried by merchants travelling the whole way between China and the Mediterranean?
answer: False. Goods moved in relays: most traders worked a stretch of a few hundred kilometres between oases, and wares changed hands many times. Documents from Niya and Turfan show mostly small, local exchanges, often by barter. A bolt of silk reaching Syria had crossed Asia without any one trader carrying it all the way.
move: A route on a map says nothing about who walked all of it.
ask: Which route or chain do I picture as one journey when many hands carried it in pieces?
trap: Picturing a single caravan, the image every map and travel tale gives.
reference: Hansen, The Silk Road: A New History, Oxford University Press, 2012
